timestamp_note: This is when matched_burn.py analyze() computed the fields it produces (n_trials, confab_rate, combined_auroc, combined_accuracy, permutation_p). It is NOT when this file was last edited. The bootstrap_* fields and every *_note/WARNING string below were hand-added on 2026-07-28 and revised on 2026-08-29 without re-running analyze(), so the single 'timestamp' field understated the file's age by five weeks and then by three months. Round-7 review, item 9.
combined_auroc_STATUS: RETRACTED. In-sample GroupKFold point estimate: one pooled fit over all 90 trials, scored on the same trials, with no interval. Superseded by the bootstrap. DO NOT CITE. Current published value: full classifier AUROC 0.9288, 95% CI [0.8192, 0.9886]. As of 2026-08-29 code/matched_burn.py prints a retraction banner at the point of computation and labels this key on write, so a re-run can no longer reproduce this number silently (round-6/round-7 review, item 5).
combined_accuracy_STATUS: RETRACTED. Same in-sample fit as combined_auroc.
permutation_p_STATUS: matched_burn.py runs n_perm=200, so the finest resolvable non-zero p is 1/200 = 0.005. The recorded 0.0 means 'below that floor', not an exact zero. The paper's stated permutation p=0.001 requires >=1000 shuffles and is NOT produced by any script in this repository.
bootstrap_note: Bootstrap over 1000 resamples with GroupKFold inside each resample, produced by code/shore_up_tests.py test 4 (test_4_bootstrap_ci). This, not combined_auroc, is the estimator behind the paper's headline. The paper reports the full classifier at AUROC 0.9288, 95% CI [0.8192, 0.9886], and an encoding-only classifier at AUROC 0.9377, 95% CI [0.8356, 0.9941]. NOTE: no script in this repository computes the encoding-only figure or a permutation p at 1000+ shuffles; those come from an unshipped refit (round-7 review, BLOCKER-1). The bootstrap_auroc_mean/ci_95 recorded above are the values from the 2026-07-28 authoring run; see bootstrap_reproduction below for what the same unmodified script produces on a different library stack.

bootstrap_reproduction.note: The shipped script prints 3 decimals; the paper states 4 (0.9288 / [0.8192, 0.9886]). Those 4-decimal digits are reproduced by nothing in this repository. Recorded here so the author-vs-reproducer gap is a documented number rather than an appeal to 'library drift' (round-6 remediation #10, round-7 vetting on Phase-0.5 row 1). The seed is fixed (np.random.seed(42)), so this gap is not sampling noise.

STALE_WARNING: combined_auroc=0.9995 is the RETRACTED in-sample result. The paper reports the full classifier at bootstrap AUROC 0.9288, 95% CI [0.8192, 0.9886], reproduced (to 3 decimals) by shore_up_tests.py test 4. Until 2026-08-29 this warning still named 0.93 [0.82, 0.98] -- numbers the paper had already abandoned -- so the annotation whose whole job is to prevent a stale number from being quoted had itself gone stale, and six commits rewrote the paper's numbers without revisiting it (round-7 review, items 4 and 12). THE POINT OF THIS KEY IS TO STOP THAT: if the paper's headline AUROC changes, this string and bootstrap_note must change in the same commit.
ANNOTATION_MAINTENANCE: Every key ending in _note, _STATUS, WARNING, or MAINTENANCE in this file is hand-written and is NOT recomputed by any script. matched_burn.py's write_analysis() carries them forward on re-run and refuses to overwrite this file without --overwrite-analysis, but nothing verifies that they are still TRUE. They are checked by a human, or not at all.
